title: The Time God Killed 70,000 People Over One Sin
paragraphs:
The Time God Killed 70,000 People Over One Sin
2 Samuel 24:15

David wanted numbers.
Not God.

He counted fighting men like victory could be measured.
Like security could be stored in human strength.
Like the kingdom stood because of armies... not because of the Lord.
And in one terrifying moment, heaven answered.

A plague swept through Israel.
From morning until the appointed time, 70,000 men fell.
Not because God is cruel.
But because sin is never small when it is committed against a holy God.
That is the part we want to skip.

We call it “just a census.”
God called it rebellion.

Because beneath David’s counting was something darker:
pride.
self-reliance.
the illusion that man can preserve himself without God.
And that is still our sin.

You trust the bank account.
The platform.
The career.
The backup plan.
The image.
The applause.
You count what you can control and forget the God who holds your breath.

Then the judgment came.
And David finally said what broken men say when God exposes them:
“I have sinned greatly.”
That is where the story turns.
Because the God who judges sin is also the God who provides mercy.

When the angel of destruction reached Jerusalem, God said,
“Enough.”

David was told to build an altar.
A sacrifice would be offered.
Blood would stand where wrath had been.
Do you see it?

This was never just about David.
This was pointing forward.

Because one day, judgment would not stop at an altar made of stone.
It would fall on Jesus Christ.

You and I have sinned far more deeply than a census.
All have sinned and fallen short of the glory of God.
The wages of sin is death.
We are not basically good people needing inspiration.
We are guilty sinners standing under holy judgment.

But Jesus Christ—fully God and fully man—lived the sinless life we never could live.
He died in the place of sinners.
He rose again on the third day.
Salvation is not earned by works, effort, religion, or moral cleanup.
It is the gift of God, received by grace through faith in Christ alone.

David’s altar stayed the plague for a moment.
Jesus’ cross is enough forever.

So repent.
Turn from your sin.
Stop trusting what you can count.
Stop hiding behind strength that cannot save you.
Believe in Jesus Christ.

This is for the one who looks strong outside but knows judgment would be deserved if God exposed everything.
This is for the one exhausted from trying to hold life together without surrendering to Christ.
